*.description: Synthetic 10T MoE with latent KV. No DeepSeek/Kimi/GLM architecture or real 2 TB HBM device is claimed.
Synthetic 10T MoE with latent KV. No DeepSeek/Kimi/GLM architecture or real 2 TB HBM device is claimed.

assumptions: Fixed ragged batch; finished sequences leave decode but no new requests arrive.
EP lanes own round-robin sequences; uniform expert routing and balanced expert compute.
Dense parameters are replicated over EP; expert parameters are sharded over EP.
Expert HBM reads use expected distinct experts touched by uniform top-k routing; active_params controls FLOPs.
Per-layer parameters are uniform within dense/expert layer categories.
Standard KV shards heads (ceil); latent KV is replicated across TP ranks.
TP boundary hidden states are replicated; PP and MoE messages carry full hidden vectors per TP lane.
Weights are preloaded; cold-start weight loading and request queueing are excluded.
Attention is fused/streaming: quadratic score matrices are not resident.
KV read precision conversion is fused into attention; new KV storage conversion has an explicit kernel and buffer.
Engram table is replicated on each participating host; cache_bytes is per participating NPU.
TP attention and FFN reductions are serialized at layer end; this is a coarse operator schedule.

topology.clos_model: one deterministic spine; uplinks share capacity

model_metadata.parameterization: Declared parameter budgets with coarse layer kernels; not an exact framework tensor trace.

communication.classification_note: Semantic and collective breakdowns are two views of the same payload; do not add them.

estimate.memory_note: Resident memory is a necessary bound; optimistic schedule peaks ignore contention/slots and are not feasibility proofs.

metrics.slo_aggregation: Maximum per-sequence TTFT and mean TPOT in a fixed batch; no arrival queue.

requirements.window_note: Whole-workload step/throughput deadline only; TTFT/TPOT have different subgraph windows. Average rates are necessary, not sufficient.

cache_mte.level: Operator footprints and access/transfer demand; not L1/L2/L3 capacity or MTE queue/channel predictions.
